pretreatments.description: Solar photocatalytic deflocculation using TiO2/chitosan thin film (TCTF) embedded in the sludge substrate. This treatment involves impregnating TiO2 nanoparticles into a chitosan nanocomposite matrix, followed by solar irradiation to facilitate exopolymer (EPS) removal. The process utilizes an optimized dosage of TiO2 (0.05 g/g SS) and chitosan to disrupt microbial aggregates, reduce turbidity, and expose microbial cells for subsequent enzymatic action. The deflocculation efficiency was optimized to ensure complete disruption of EPS layers, resulting in a 99.35% deflocculation degree within 25 minutes, which allows for effective exposure of microbial cells for bacterial disintegration.

Enzyme secreting bacterial disintegration of deflocculated sludge. This pretreatment utilizes specific bacterial strains isolated and identified as Bacillus jerish 03 (Accession number: KC597266) and Bacillus jerish 04 (Accession number: KC597267). The treated sludge is incubated at 40 °C under constant mixing for 42 hours at a pH of 6.5. This process releases protease and amylase enzymes from the bacterial cells to solubilize particulate organic matter. The treatment significantly enhances SS reduction from 3914.58 mg/L to 3500 mg/L, increases COD solubilization efficiency to 16%, and promotes maximum intracellular substance release (Protein: 452.48 mg/L, Carbohydrate: 290.88 mg/L) before anaerobic digestion.
